More than 400 U.K. entertainment industry professionals have signed an open letter, released Monday, calling on leaders at studios, broadcasters and unions to end the culture of silence and secrecy that the signatories say allowed Russell Brand ’s abuse to go unchecked. Brand was sentenced last week to 10 and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault.

The letter, billed as an “open letter to the creative industry, from the creative industry,” comes as Little Britain star David Walliams faces allegations of sexual misconduct. A joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News includes accounts from two women who say Walliams groomed them after meeting them when they were 15. Walliams denies wrongdoing. The letter asks those in power to “review your processes, protect those who speak out and become less offended by your inaction being named than you are by the actions you are being asked to recognize.” Related Stories General News Brit List 2026: Cornwall Outlaw Series, Coming-of-Age Film Top List of Unproduced Film, TV Scripts Movies Dual Oscar Winner Christopher Hampton Calls Glenn Close Honorary Oscar "the Least They Can Do," Says AI Is Just "a Super Google"

The letter was written by writer-actor-producer Ben Fletcher, co-organized by Alexa Morden and published on a dedicated website, makethisaturningpoint.com. Signatories include actors, directors and producers such as Natalie Dormer ( Game of Thrones , The Hunger Games ) and Richard Armitage ( The Hobbit ). The letter calls on the government to “act, not debate” by “increasing support for victims, ensuring police forces are fully resourced, and forcing accountability for those who know but choose convenient ignorance.”

Brand’s sentencing on Nov. 9, after a high-profile London trial in which he testified in his own defense, is a major catalyst for the letter. But the letter opens with a warning against calling this moment a turning point for a problem that has plagued the entertainment industry for decades.

“To afford such a label would be to ignore that it has taken some 17 years for justice,” it reads. The letter adds that one witness in Brand’s trial received death threats online, and that during the trial his lawyer threatened the reporter who uncovered his crimes.

On Monday, Brand released a statement through his wife , Laura Brand, who appeared to hold back tears as she read his claim of innocence in a video posted to YouTube. Britain’s Justice Secretary Alex Norris called the broadcast of a statement from Brand while in prison “completely unacceptable.”

entertainment.title: Lawsuit Accusing Selena Gomez and Wondermind Co-Founders of Fraud Is Dismissed
entertainment.summary: A lawyer for Gomez said the star "looks forward to putting the matter behind her"
entertainment.body:
A lawsuit accusing Selena Gomez , her mother Mandy Teefey, and The Newsette founder, Daniella Pierson, of defrauding investors behind the mental health startup Wondermind has been dropped after her attorneys filed a motion to dismiss the case.

“Selena is pleased by today’s dismissal of the case following our motion to dismiss and looks forward to putting the matter behind her,” her lawyer Mathew S. Rosengart said in a statement to Rolling Stone. According to documents, the plaintiffs “voluntarily” dismissed the lawsuit.

An attorney for Pierson, Scott Balber, told Billboard that they did not pay any settlement in the case. “Ms. Pierson did nothing wrong,” said Balber. “Apparently, the plaintiff recognized that and dismissed the complaint against her. Unfortunately, Ms. Pierson’s reputation has already been damaged by these false allegations. We are hopeful that the dismissal of the lawsuit will be the first step in restoring her good name.”

In August, Gomez, Teefey, and Pierson were sued by investors claiming they pumped nearly $1.2 million into Wondermind, which launched in 2021, and were fed false promises about the company’s infrastructure, leadership, and resources as the company collapsed. The trio, who founded the startup, were sued for securities fraud, common law fraud, and breach of contract.

entertainment.body:
Luke Grimes initially struggled to imagine his “Yellowstone” character’s future without his on-screen wife — and now “Marshals” is exploring whether Kayce Dutton could find love again.

Speaking to ScreenRant, Grimes revealed that reprising his role without Kelsey Asbille, who played Monica Dutton throughout “Yellowstone,” was one of his biggest concerns about the spinoff.

“Marshals” picks up after the events of “Yellowstone,” with Kayce and his son, Tate, grieving Monica’s death.

Speaking to ScreenRant , Grimes admitted that one of his biggest concerns before agreeing to a “Yellowstone” spinoff was doing it without Asbille.

“The thing I was most worried about doing ‘Marshals’ was doing it without Kelsey. That’s legitimate. Like I just couldn’t wrap my head around Kayce without Monica. That was the story. The rest of ‘Yellowstone’ was about people fighting over land, and I just loved my wife,” Grimes said. “I had my own thing going on, and so I didn’t know what that would even look like.”

Grimes continued, “But then once I sort of, you know, could wrap my head around the fact that that was going to open up all these new storylines, like, we just have to make sure we do honor that and don’t try to skip over it or pretend it didn’t happen.”

Now in its second season, “Marshals” is exploring Kayce’s growing bond with fellow U.S. Marshal Andrea Cruz, played by Ash Santos, raising the possibility of romance as he continues to grieve Monica.

Speaking to ScreenRant, Grimes addressed fans’ concerns, saying that they are meant to feel that way.

entertainment.title: Tallinn Market Debates Estonia’s Film Sector and How Foreign Shoots “Bring Both Value and Tension”
entertainment.summary: Also in focus was data on how many local films screened in the Baltic nation's cinemas in 2025 and more.
entertainment.body:
The Estonian film industry may be small but has big ambitions. And there is more that the Baltic country’s institutions can and must do to make the sector more sustainable as it balances big foreign productions visiting and local work. Those were key messages of an event at the 25th edition of the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event (ITBE) market, part of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF).

Lennart Mathias Männik and Kätlin Palm presented findings from their master’s theses. Among the data findings was that 74 Estonian films screened in the nation’s cinemas in 2025. “It’s not all new films. It’s films in general,” Männik shared. “And looking at our market and looking at our country size, it’s quite an achievement.” Related Stories Movies Dual Oscar Winner Christopher Hampton Calls Glenn Close Honorary Oscar "the Least They Can Do," Says AI Is Just "a Super Google" Music IVE, BINI, KiiiKiii, SB19, LiSA and Babymetal Score Grammy Nominations in New Asian Pop Category

Admissions for Estonian films last year hit 334,471, making the domestic share of cinema admissions in Estonia account for 14 percent. The by far biggest public funding support came from the Estonian Film Institute at €10.9 million ($12.0 million), followed by the Cultural Endowment at €3.1 million ($3.4 million) and €1.7 million ($1.9 million).

Männik’s conclusion: Estonia has “a small domestic market, but a visible national cinema with an audience.” But he summarized what he sees as key for the future outlook this way: “building a stronger, more sustainable Estonian film industry.”

Two key areas that need to be addressed: “underfunding limits production and creative freedom is under pressure” due to a lack of development resources and “rigid or unclear support expectations,” which can lead to creative caution.

Last but not least, foreign projects “bring both value and tension,” Männik highlighted. “Service productions [from abroad] bring investment, work and expertise but draw on the same limited workforce as domestic films. Without stronger local production capacity, international growth can leave Estonian films more vulnerable.”

Among the foreign films and series shot in Estonia have been the likes of Paramount+ spy thriller series The Agency and Tenet .

His suggestions for the Estonian sector and its support: adopt a long-term audiovisual strategy, make funding more diverse and stable, and strengthen the whole production ecosystem.

entertainment.title: Selena Gomez No Longer Facing Lawsuit Over Mental Health Startup Wondermind
entertainment.summary: A lawyer for Gomez, who was sued alongside her mother and former company exec Daniella Pierson, says she "looks forward to putting this matter behind her."
entertainment.body:
Investors in Selena Gomez ’s mental health startup Wondermind have dropped their fraud lawsuit against the star and company.

A Monday (Nov. 16) court notice, obtained and first reported by Billboard , says that five investors are permanently dismissing the claims they brought in August against Wondermind, Gomez, her mother Mandy Teefey and former company executive Daniella Pierson . Gomez’s attorney, Mathew Rosengart , told Billboard on Monday, “Selena is pleased by the dismissal of the case on the heels of our motion to dismiss on her behalf, and looks forward to putting this matter behind her.”

A lawyer for Pierson, Scott Balber , told Billboard on Monday that they did not pay any settlement in the case. “Ms. Pierson did nothing wrong,” said Balber. “Apparently, the plaintiff recognized that and dismissed the complaint against her. Unfortunately, Ms. Pierson’s reputation has already been damaged by these false allegations. We are hopeful that the dismissal of the lawsuit will be the first step in restoring her good name.”

Teefey and the investors’ attorneys did not immediately return requests for comment.

Wondermind launched in 2021 with Teefey and Pierson as co-CEOs and public support from Gomez. The plan was for the company to host a suite of mental health media initiatives, including a digital magazine, mobile app and podcast.

An investment vehicle run by five men — Brent Saunders , Marc Roberts , EJ Solimine , Andrew Resnick and Mark Peikin — put $1.2 million into Wondermind in 2022. In the August lawsuit, the investors alleged they were duped by false promises that Gomez would be actively involved as Wondermind’s head of marketing, thus leveraging her huge fanbase and 400 million Instagram followers. They were also allegedly told that Wondermind had a “potential future valuation” of more than $4 billion and solid brand partnerships in place already.

Last year, The Cut published a bombshell investigation reporting that Gomez had distanced herself from Wondermind and that the company’s finances were in dire condition, due in part to Teefey’s alleged substance abuse issues and erratic behavior. According to the lawsuit, this article led the investors to believe they’d been defrauded. They asked for their money back and, when it didn’t come, resorted to litigation.

Gomez’s team was quick to argue that she did not belong in the lawsuit. Rosengart called the case “absurd” in court papers, saying Gomez had no involvement in Wondermind’s fundraising operations and “should never have been dragged into this action.”

entertainment.title: Brad Pitt Explains Why Leonardo DiCaprio’s Cameo in ‘Cliff Booth’ Movie Fell Apart
entertainment.summary: The actor told The Hollywood Reporter at the L.A. premiere that a Rick Dalton appearance in the sequel would have "required a lot of prosthetics."
entertainment.body:
Though Brad Pitt and Leonardo DiCaprio both starred in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood , only Pitt appears in the sequel, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth — and the star is shedding some light on why.

Cliff Booth is a follow-up to 2019’s Once Upon a Time , this time centered on Pitt’s stuntman character and set eight years after Quentin Tarantino’s original film. Tarantino wrote the script for the new film with David Fincher taking over as director, and DiCaprio confirmed to Deadline last year that his leading man Rick Dalton is not along for the ride this time, even in a cameo capacity. Related Stories News John Oliver Fills in for Tom Papa at Michael J. Fox Foundation Gala After FAA Ground Stop Lifestyle Baby2Baby Gala Fetes Demi Moore and Raises Over $20M for the Cause

“There were some talks about it early on. Ultimately, I cannot wait to see the Cliff Booth story, but I’m not in it,” he told the outlet. “I think David Fincher’s the perfect man for the job. Quentin is a huge fan of his work, I’m a huge fan of his work, and there’s nobody better to carry on that lineage and tell that story. I think it’s the next phase of Cliff Booth’s life. I’m excited to see it.”

At the Los Angeles premiere on Monday, Pitt told The Hollywood Reporter that a DiCaprio appearance “would have been great fun, but it required a lot of prosthetics, which is a good couple of weeks prepping to get him. It’s hardly worth the cost for a cameo.” There is a joke in the traile r where Booth explains he no longer doubles for DiCaprio’s character because “Rick got too fat,” which is likely where prosthetics would have come into play.

“It was talked about for a while, but it just seemed like a big ask,” he added, teasing that they still make a couple of “sweet tributes” to Rick Dalton in the sequel.

Both Pitt and DiCaprio earned Oscar nominations for their Once Upon a Time performances, with Pitt going on to win. The follow-up film sees Cliff Booth having left Rick and his stunt career behind, working as a bartender, a projectionist and a Hollywood fixer in the town’s dark underbelly. Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller round out the cast.

Also on the carpet, Pitt said he did not expect to reprise the character, but “Quentin was talking about for his 10th one he wanted to do this again — his last film, as he says — and he just wanted to work with friends and do something he loved and I was really flattered. And then he went, ‘Nah!'”

For those hoping for reunion between Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson , the odds are finally in your favor.

The original Hunger Games stars walked the red carpet together for the first time in 11 years, attending the New York City premiere of the franchise's new Sunrise on the Reaping prequel on Nov. 16.

Jennifer, 36, seemed to channel series villain President Snow with her long black Christian Dior coat, as it featured a white fur collar and rose embroidery on the train, which she paired with matching open-toe heels. Meanwhile, Josh, 34, let the games begin in an all-black suit with leather boots.

But they weren't the only familiar faces to leave the crowd totally star-crossed. After all, their former castmates Woody Harrelson , Elizabeth Banks , Jena Malone , Willow Shields and Amandla Stenberg were also in attendance, posing for an epic group photo with their longtime director Francis Lawrence and The Hunger Games author Suzanne Collins .

Jennifer and Josh reprised their respective roles of Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark in Sunrise on the Reaping , a prequel starring Mckenna Grace and Joseph Zada that follows Hamish Abernathy (played by Woody in the OG series) during his time competing in 50th Hunger Games before becoming a mentor.

And for Jennifer, it was a capitol idea to return to the franchise.

"Oh man, it was unbelievable," the Oscar winner raved in an October episode of the Call Her Daddy podcast. "It was so crazy because it was the same crew. It was the same camera guys, the same [assistant director] who I've worked with a million times too, 'cause I love him."

In fact, she and Josh "didn't walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other."

entertainment.title: Wale on Triumphant Pair of 2027 Grammy Nominations for ‘Everything Is a Lot’: ‘I Hope It Teaches a Lot of People About Resilience’
entertainment.summary: "Vote for Wale. I'm gonna draft up the greatest speech of all time," the DMV rapper tells Billboard .
entertainment.body:
Wale is still training his mind to have a positive outlook when it comes to musical accolades. As a longtime fan of the snakebitten Washington Commanders and Wizards franchises, one would understand his built-in hesitancy.

However, Monday (Nov. 16) is a different story. Fresh off a flight to NYC, Folarin is riding high after earning a pair of 2027 Grammy Award nominations tied to his 2025 LP Everything Is a Lot .

The DMV rap veteran picked up his first Grammy nomination for 2011’s top 40 Billboard Hot 100 hit “Lotus Flower Bomb.” But even after a handful of multiplatinum Hot 100 hits and critically acclaimed projects, the Grammys never came calling back.

Fifteen years and six albums later, that changed Monday morning with Everything Is a Lot. notching a best rap album nomination, along with “Watching Us” — which topped the Rhythmic Airplay chart — featuring Grammy darling Leon Thomas being nominated for best melodic rap performance.

“I’m just grateful, full of gratitude,” Wale says on a call in the car, his voice a bit hoarse. “15 years was my one and only nomination. I always wondered how I would feel if I got any of these things. There’s a part of my brain that was like, ‘Man, that sh– ain’t gonna happen.’ But then there’s another part of me that was like, ‘Bro, do you realize like the one and only joint was 15 years ago?’ I don’t know if too many people could say that.”

The 42-year-old wordsmith continues: “To get it 15 years later, and then one of them to be for [best] rap album, it just it means a lot, bro. It’s like the white whale, I guess they call it, you just can’t never catch. So it just, it’s a lot of emotion. … I’m still kind of taking it all in. Like I don’t want to be that guy that’s going crazy just for a nomination, but I am.”

Wale is used to brushing off compliments about his work, but this time around he knew something felt different, pointing to a conversation with DaBaby, who showed his latest album love. “[DaBaby’s] like, ‘Man, that album.’ And I’m like, ‘OK, this is different,'” he recalls. “This ain’t just people that know me. There’s people that don’t have no reason to say this to me. But again, I still have my guard up because I didn’t want to wake up with nothing and then just be dejected. But we don’t have to worry about that no more.”

The pair of Grammy nominations fittingly came just two days after the first anniversary of Everything Is a Lot. , which Wale championed as the “most important” project of his career. His first release with Def Jam, the 2025 album debuted inside the Billboard 200 ‘s top 20 and “Watching Us,” which reached No. 76 on the Hot 100 , was the last track to make the LP’s cut.

Included in that is Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon), who carries some interesting, distinctive qualities to his character. Aside from the famous set of Gibbs rules , Gibbs has another famous trait — smacking heads. Throughout his time on the series, it's not uncommon for Gibbs to give his agents, especially Tony DiNozzo (Michael Weatherly), a good smack behind the head.

During an interview with the French publication Premiere (via Showbiz Cheat Sheet ), Mark Harmon explained the slap originated during a frustrating Season 1 shoot. Weatherly wouldn't stick to the script, and Harmon had enough of it. "I just reached over and smacked him," he told the publication. "I tried to put him back on line."

Despite the surprise, Weatherly did not break character, nor did the rest of the cast. At that moment, the iconic slap was born. "And people liked it." Harmon continued. "And every episode I was smacking him — maybe too much."

CBS It's revealed in the Season 2 finale of "NCIS: Origins" that the slap originates from a young Mike Franks (Kyle Schmid). A young Gibbs (Austin Stowell) is slapped on the back of head by Franks. Preparing for Camp Pendleton's closure, he, Bernard Randolph (Caleb Foote), and Lala Dominguez (Mariel Molino) are studying potential transfer locations for work. Franks walks in and slaps Gibbs to make an example, wanting his team to focus on the case. Franks even threatens Randolph later when he asks about a possible Italy assignment.

Gibbs justifies his habit in the "NCIS" Season 2 episode "The Bone Yard," explaining, "Slap in the face would be humiliating. Back of the head's a wake-up call." He also mentions in the Season 3 episode "Hiatus (Part 1)" that Franks introduced the idea to him. Hilariously (and characteristically), Gibbs even smacks himself sometimes.

After squashing a threat stemming from a Mexican cartel's surprising partnership with the Iranian guard, Scola makes the ultimate sacrifice for his family: He tells Nina he's going to put in for a transfer to San Diego. "You're my life," he said. "You and our son are my life. And I'm going to be wherever you are."

Below, John Boyd and Shantel VanSanten talk to TVLine about the emotional episode of "FBI," Nina's return to the series, and what Scola's big decision might mean for both the character and the man who portrays him.

TVLINE | We haven't seen Nina since the wedding, but how would you describe Scola and Nina's marriage and what makes this couple work? SHANTEL VANSANTEN | Everything that we've seen on TV for seasons and seasons before, the marriage is like the cherry on the top. They had already built such a deep partnership and commitment to one another, and a way of functioning within that relationship, [while] still pursuing the job and being two working parents who are agents, who are sacrificing constantly... this is another evolution in their life. Then, an opportunity for Nina to follow her dreams. Who's going to make the ultimate sacrifice for one another? Are you going to support? Am I going to stay? It's some of those ongoing conversations we weren't maybe privy to in the episode that lead us to the space where we find them, where we open and the moving truck is getting packed and they have a plan for how it's going to work. We'll see how that unfolds.

TVLINE | John, a couple of episodes ago, we saw Scola wrestling with the idea of Nina leaving. Should he convince her to stay? Should he encourage her to go? He was struggling a bit. How did he come around to the notion of supporting her fully and being there for her? JOHN BOYD | I think what Scola comes to in that episode is that their relationship, the foundation of the basis of their connection, is a mutual understanding of what it means to serve to a higher calling. To understand what it means to believe in the possibility of a better world, and to deny someone you love of exploring that is not only not love, but that's brutality. In their understanding of love, he realizes that he cannot require her to choose between him and what she loves to do. So, I think that's an interesting place to jump off from. The episode begins with them really not understanding what's involved, right? I'm not going to stand between you and this thing, and we'll make it work no matter what. But we don't really know if that's going to work.

entertainment.title: Snubs & Surprises in the 2027 Dance/Electronic Grammy Nominations
entertainment.summary: The nominations once again reveal the dance world's fractured factions.
entertainment.body:
The 2027 Grammy nominations were announced early Monday morning (Nov. 16), with the dance/electronic nominees setting off a dance scene debate currently blazing on social media and also happening off the record via DM, text and phone.

Let’s start with the nominees: As expected, Madonna is the leader, with her July club voyage Confessions II getting nods in all four dance categories: best dance/electronic album, best dance recording, best dance pop recording and best remixed recording. Slayyyter is a close second, with her March project Wor$t Girl In America garnering three nominations across best dance/electronic album, best dance/electronic recording and best dance pop recording.

Projects by Robyn, Skrillex and Tame Impala round out the albums category, while Fred again.., Tame Impala, Tinashe and Underscores make up the rest of the best dance/electronic recording nominees.

One person who isn’t nominated is John Summit , who tweeted his irritation with the nominees this morning, writing that he’s “Never submitting to the grammys again unless s–t changes, it’s all a f–king joke.” He then wrote, “i’m not just talking about myself either there’s zero respect for real electronic dance music and djs. the whole dance category is just music industry fueled pop stars.”

The tweet got a few notable replies, including one from Charli xcx, who quoted-tweeted Summit and wrote “not this guy again!” The producer nightfeelings also responded to the tweet saying that he worked on Tinashe’s Melatonin and that “I actually come from dance music, my first project released on the same labels as Aphex Twin, I’ve performed at Berghain, Andy Weatherall played my tune Cheaters in every set for awhile. I made a song with Romanthony. Just gonna leave that there.”

So, there’s a lot to unpack here, particularly in regard to what “real electronic dance music and djs” even means. In a notoriously gatekeeping genre, this sentiment highlights the reality that the dance world isn’t a cohesive ecosystem of likeminded pals. Instead, it’s a loosely defined global scene made up of a dizzying taxonomy of subgenres that are all (sometimes unhappily) living together under a “dance/electronic” umbrella that covers styles that sound nothing like each other and includes artists who might never want to be on a lineup together.

This scope means that certain – and in fact most – areas of dance music are left out of the Grammys conversation, despite how popular they might be within their respective scenes.

sports.title: Derrick Henry on 10 carries for 10 yards: I don't have an answer, just not good enough
sports.summary: Overall, the Ravens totaled 15 carries for 16 yards, their lowest rushing output in more than 10 years.
sports.body:
Henry gained just 10 yards on 10 carries, and another 10 yards on five catches. Afterward he said he couldn’t explain what went wrong in a 23-20 loss to the Chargers.

“I don’t know. I don’t have no answer. Guys who are out there are healthy, trying to do their jobs, we just ain’t good enough,” Henry said.

Overall, the Ravens totaled 15 carries for 16 yards, their lowest rushing yardage output in more than 10 years. Henry did run for two touchdowns, but he also had five plays on which he got no gain or negative yardage. Asked if the absence of quarterback Lamar Jackson is the problem, Henry said the players who are there have to take responsibility.

“We just haven’t been executing. Of course Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it’s a grown-man league,” Henry said. “We just haven’t been doing our jobs good enough, it hasn’t been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that. Of course having 8 would help, but at the end of the day, we’ve got to go out there and do our jobs.”

The Ravens are 4-6 and the season appears to be slipping away, but Henry said he’ll always believe they can turn the season around.

“I’m never not gonna believe that we can turn it around and play the way we want to play,” Henry said. “You’ve still got to go to work. The season is still going to be here, you’ve still got to play. None of us are going to be like, ‘Let’s lose the rest of them.’ You’ve still got to do your best.”

sports.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning concludes his fourth slate of home games with the Longhorns on Saturday.
sports.body:
The only clue, if it even is one, comes from his decision to participate in the Texas Senior Day.

“ I’m a senior, so I’m doing it ,” Manning said, via the Associated Press.

So what’s next after he participates in the traditional farewell home game?

“I’m not really thinking about the future right now,” Manning said.

The future entails three primary options: (1) enter the draft; (2) return to Texas; or (3) transfer.

Manning started the year as the favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. That has changed.

Last year, he had 26 touchdown passes and seven interceptions for the Longhorns, who finished 10-3 for a team that did not qualify for the College Football Playoff. This year, Manning has 19 touchdown passes and 10 interceptions through 10 games. Texas currently is No. 6 in the CFP rankings.

After two straight losses (to Oklahoma and Florida), coach Steve Sarkisian didn’t rule out benching Manning.

sports.title: Monday Night Football: Chargers run past Ravens 23-20 for first win of 2026
sports.summary: The Chargers outrushed the Ravens 160 to 16.
sports.body:
By the time Brissett got the ball back, the Ravens were in need of a miracle, and his Hail Mary on the final play fell incomplete.

The Chargers won for the first time, holding off the Ravens 23-20. Los Angeles is 1-8, while Baltimore lost its fifth in a row to fall to 4-6.

The Chargers led from start to finish, winning for the first time since Week 16 of 2025 when they beat the Cowboys. They twice had a double-digit lead in the second half.

Brissett, acquired in a trade from the Cardinals last week, went 33-of-49 for 340 yards and an interception. It was his most passing yards since Week 11 of last season when he threw for 452 yards for the Cardinals against the 49ers.

He had no help from the running game, which contributed 16 yards on 15 carries. Derrick Henry had 10 yards and two touchdowns on 10 carries.

Mark Andrews caught eight passes for 82 yards and Flowers had six catches for 74 yards.

The Ravens outgained the Chargers 347 to 287, but Los Angeles gained 160 yards on the ground.

With 1:52 left, Justin Herbert completed an 11-yard pass to Charlie Kolar for a first down. The Chargers ended up punting, but the Ravens had only 11 seconds from their own 20. Brissett threw a 21-yard pass to Ja’Kobi Lane before R.J. Mickens knocked down a Hail Mary attempt intended for Lane to end the game.

sports.title: Derrick Henry's second TD has Ravens back within a FG
sports.summary: Derrick Henry has 10 carries for 10 yards, but he has two touchdowns.
sports.body:
His second one has pulled the Ravens within 23-20 of the Chargers.

The Chargers have twice had double-digit second-half leads at 20-10 and 23-13. It’s the first time the Chargers have had a double-digit lead in the second half since beating the Cowboys 34-17 in Week 16 last season. That was Los Angeles’ last win.

The Ravens, though, have made it a game despite only 15 rushing yards.

Jacoby Brissett, making his first start with the Ravens, is 25-of-39 for 280 yards and an interception.

He led the Ravens on a 10-play, 71-yard drive that has them back within a field goal.

The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) and list right guard Vega Ioane as questionable with a left shoulder injury. Ioane played through it into the second half before Chuma Edoga replaced him.

sports.title: Rex Ryan politicks for job with Cowboys
sports.summary: Rex Ryan is plenty of things.
sports.body:
Days after being arrested for allegedly running over the feet of two people in Nashville with his pickup truck and fleeing the scene, Ryan is on the air — and he’s using the bully pulpit to politick for a job with the Cowboys.

“I could go there today and say, ‘Alright, we can have an average ass defense,’” Ryan said on ESPN New York, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing . “I’ll promise you they’d be average, I’d probably make them top-10 . But I’ll take that group right now, in one week, I’d go in and turn this thing out.”

Ryan’s pitch came after he ripped the current defensive coaching staff in Dallas.

“It’s the worst coached defense I’ve ever seen,” Ryan said. “It really is. And I’ve seen some horrible defenses, this one’s awful, and it starts with coaching. . . . They make more mental mistakes than any defense I’ve seen, as well as the physical, they’re not a tough physical defense.”

As noted separately by Michael McCarthy of Front Office Sports, Ryan also criticized the Dallas defense on ESPN’s Get Up.

“ It starts with the young guy they hired , Christian Parker,” Ryan said. “What on his resume told you he was going to be a good defensive coordinator candidate for a team like the Dallas Cowboys with Super Bowl aspirations? By the way, what told you anything about him that would make you think he could be a leader in this? Because you better hire a leader for that spot.”

(It would have been great if someone else on the show would have said, “Yeah, the Cowboys defense is extremely pedestrian.”)

“To me, absolute garbage,” Ryan said. “You can’t fire them all yet, but you damn sure better. To me, it’s the whole defensive staff. It’s not just Christian Parker. It’s not. It’s every one of those coaches on defense.”

sports.title: NFL Honors moves from Thursday back to Saturday
sports.summary: The NFL Honors ceremony is on the move, again.
sports.body:
The made-for-TV awards show, which shifts this year from broadcast to streaming, will also be sliding back to its original day.

John Ourand of Puck reports that NFL Honors will be held not on the Thursday of Super Bowl week but on the Saturday of Super Bowl weekend. The show slid to Thursday in 2022.

Netflix has acquired the rights to the show, which attracted 3.7 million viewers in February 2026.

During the event, the various Associated Press awards are announced. Also, the new class of Hall of Famers is unveiled.

As NFL programming goes, the numbers aren’t great. As live TV goes, three million people at one time is nothing to sneeze at. Whether Netflix will realize that kind of audience remains to be seen — if the official figure is even disclosed.

Regardless, the show will quickly be forgotten as the NFL pivots the next day to the biggest event of the year.

sports.title: Dolphins DT Zeek Biggers out for the season with knee injury
sports.summary: Dolphins defensive tackle Zeek Biggers will require season-ending surgery to repair his lateral meniscus, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.
sports.body:
Biggers’ injury comes a week after Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler ruptured his biceps, and defensive tackle Jordan Phillips injured his arm in Sunday’s loss to the Colts.

Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. are the only healthy defensive tackles left on the 53-player roster. Third-year defensive tackle Jordan Jefferson is on the practice squad.

In 2026, he played all nine games, with two starts, and totaled 18 tackles, a sack and a pass deflection.

sports.title: Monday Night Football: Chargers lead Ravens 17-10 at halftime
sports.summary: Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton have touchdown runs for the winless Chargers.
sports.body:
They scored 23 against Seattle and 22 last week against Houston.

Los Angeles scored on 3-of-5 first-half possessions, getting a 22-yard touchdown run from Justin Herbert, a 38-yard Cameron Dicker field goal and a 1-yard Omarion Hampton touchdown run.

Hampton’s touchdown came on fourth-and-goal with 1:56 remaining in the half. Roquan Smith initially had Hampton stopped before the running back got a push from offensive lineman Cole Strange and a pull from fullback Scott Matlock. Officials should have penalized Matlock for the pull, as pulling is illegal.

The Chargers outgained the Ravens 175 to 161, with Baltimore having no rushing yards on six carries.

Herbert, who injured his left hand in last week’s loss to the Texans but wasn’t on the injury report this week, went 6-for-9 for 91 yards in the first half. He also ran for 45 yards on six carries.

Hampton has 36 yards on 10 carries, and Tre’ Harris has five catches for 86 yards.

Jacoby Brissett, making his first start for the Ravens after the trade from Arizona, has completed 14 of 23 passes for 163 yards and an interception. Del’Shawn Phillips had the pick on a pass that was behind Ja’Kobi Lane and deflected to the Chargers linebacker.

Derrick Henry has a 2-yard touchdown run, but he has minus-1 yard on five carries. Mark Andrews has four catches for 41 yards.

sports.title: Von Miller blames himself, not the play call, for Christian McCaffrey's late TD
sports.summary: The Cowboys pulled within 38-32 of the 49ers with 3:42 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday.
sports.body:
Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is under fire for calling cover zero on second-and-10. He sent a six-man blitz, leaving man-to-man coverage and Von Miller matched up with McCaffrey.

The running back ran a seam route, quickly got a step (or two or three) on the 37-year-old edge rusher, caught the ball at the 40 and was off to the races. Miller reached 18.5 mph while chasing McCaffrey, but it wasn’t fast enough.

Miller, though, defended Parker and the play call on Monday.

“As a defensive coordinator in that situation, you want to be aggressive ,” Miller said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “We were trying to win the game. We were trying to create momentum. We were down by six points. If we could have just got off the field. . . . As a defensive coordinator, you want to be aggressive and want to win the game. That’s the type of mindset you want in these games.”

Parker is three years younger than Miller, but has Miller’s full support despite the struggles of the Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed 584 yards to the 49ers.

“Nah, that’s crazy,” Miller said of the calls for Parker’s job. “Christian is an incredible leader of men. All of these offensive and defensive coordinators are geniuses. It’s really getting your players to buy in. What happened with me yesterday is a microcosm of what has happened the whole season. Instead of me looking for a simpler way to do that job, I have to find a better way to do it. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I had been coached on how to play that route. I’ve had examples of that route, went over that play in practice this week. I just didn’t make that play. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I just didn’t execute.”

sports.title: Derrick Henry draws Ravens to within 10-7 of Chargers
sports.summary: The Ravens are on the board.
sports.body:
Derrick Henry ran for a 2-yard touchdown behind Vega Ioane to get the home team within 10-7 of the Chargers.

It was Henry’s ninth rushing touchdown of the season and 131st of his career.

Jacoby Brissett, making his first start for the Ravens since they acquired him from Arizona, finally found some rhythm on the team’s fourth possession. The Ravens went three-and-out on their first three possessions.

Brissett, though, had throws of 10 yards to Mark Andrews on third-and-10, 17 yards to Zay Flowers, 16 yards to Andrews and 24 yards to Rashod Bateman.

Brissett, the team’s fourth starter of the season, is 8-of-13 for 81 yards.

sports.title: Texans estimate David Montgomery as a full participant, but Woody Marks doesn't practice
sports.summary: The Texans did not practice on Monday, but they were required to release an injury report ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
sports.body:
Running back David Montgomery was estimated as a full participant again, putting him on track to return this week. A groin injury has sidelined him the past four games.

Montgomery returned to practice Thursday and was a full participant Friday, but he was inactive again Sunday.

The Texans estimated linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin), wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring), tight end Brevin Jordan (foot/illness) and running back Woody Marks (concussion) as non-participants. Al-Shaair, Harrison, Hunter and Jordan did not play Sunday, and Marks was hurt in the loss to the Browns.

Linebacker Jake Hummel (groin) was listed as limited Monday.

Safety Reed Blankenship (hand), wide receiver Tank Dell (hand/shoulder), offensive tackle Blake Fisher (thumb), cornerback Kamari Lassiter (wrist), offensive guard Febechi Nwaiwu (knee), offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (shoulder), cornerback Jaylin Smith (hamstring) and offensive guard Wyatt Teller (back) were full participants.

sports.title: Justin Herbert runs for 22-yard TD, giving Chargers a 7-0 lead
sports.summary: Justin Herbert's left hand seems just fine.
sports.body:
The Chargers quarterback ran for a 22-yard touchdown, his first rushing touchdown since Week 9 of last season.

The Chargers have struggled to score this season, but had no problem moving the ball on their first drive of the night.

After the Ravens went three-and-out with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, the Chargers drove 63 yards in only six plays. Omarion Hampton had runs of 11, 4 and 4 yards and recovered his own fumble on the second one.

Herbert was 1-of-2 for 22 yards, with Tre’ Harris getting the only reception.

Herbert injured his left hand in last week’s loss to the Texans, but was not on the injury report this week.

sports.title: Baltimore Ravens vs. Los Angeles Chargers, ‘MNF’ Week 10 fan discussion
sports.summary: Okay Rumblers, it’s time for another amazing NFL matchup in primetime, this time featuring the Baltimore Ravens taking on the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Week 10 of Monday Night Football. It’s unfortunate this game isn’t a better-on-paper matchup since it’s been rare this season to see an AFC-e
sports.body: Okay Rumblers, it’s time for another amazing NFL matchup in primetime, this time featuring the Baltimore Ravens taking on the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Week 10 of Monday Night Football. It’s unfortunate this game isn’t a better-on-paper matchup since it’s been rare this season to see an AFC-exclusive game. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett makes his debut for the Ravens tonight, and the fan base hopes he can save a season that feels lost without injured quarterback Lamar Jackson. Brissett and Baltimore would be wise to lean on Derrick Henry and a rushing attack that can still hurt any defense in the NFL. As for the Chargers, well… it’s ugly. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has been brutal and the team in general just can’t get out of its own way. Unfortunately, quarterback Justin Herbert is stuck on a team that refuses to set him free. Soon enough, he may be able to breathe a sigh of relief if the front office proves merciful enough to dismiss McDaniel and head coach John Harbaugh. The game has proven too big for both, at least in LA. Here’s your open thread for Week 10 of Monday Night football. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.title: Andy Reid defends Xavier Worthy, who had no catches in 57 snaps
sports.summary: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed 22 passes to eight different receivers and threw five touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
sports.body:
Worthy has 33 catches for 278 yards and a touchdown in nine games this season. The Chiefs have not used him in the run game.

On Sunday, he led all Kansas City wide receivers with 57 snaps and drew three targets. He also made a special teams mistake, allowing the Falcons to recover the first successful onside kick of the season in the NFL.

Coach Andy Reid was asked about Worthy’s lack of production, which had to be at least part of the reason the Chiefs traded for Josh Downs last week. Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Kansas City debut.

“He just needs to keep doing his thing and working, and he’ll be fine ,” Reid said Monday, via Charles Goldman of AtoZ Sports. “Some days will be his, and some days it goes to other guys. I mean, that’s just how this thing works. We’re spreading it around. Pat loves spreading it around and does a great job with it. Our coaches love doing that. It’s tough on defenses. Everybody’s kind of getting a little piece of the pie. You saw when he was only the guy against the Chargers and his production there was great. So, it’s not that he’s not capable of that.”

Reid further explained that the Falcons’ game plan was to take Worthy out of the game, which “allowed other guys to be available.”

Worthy, a first-round pick in 2024, had his best season as a rookie when he made 59 catches for 638 yards and six touchdowns, while also running for 104 yards and three touchdowns on 20 carries.

In the 23 games he’s played since, Worthy has 75 catches for 810 yards and two touchdowns, with 11 carries for 87 yards and no touchdowns.

sports.title: Monday Night Football: No surprises among Chargers-Ravens inactives
sports.summary: The Chargers will officially see the return of tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman.
sports.body:
Njoku (fibula) has not played since Week 2, and he has six catches for 67 yards.

The Chargers’ inactives are wide receiver Ladd McConkey (back), safety Kendall Williamson (calf), cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), outside linebacker Bud Dupree, wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) and defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle).

The Ravens’ inactives are safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), wide receiver Elijah Sarratt, cornerback Chandler Rivers, offensive guard Emery Jones, defensive tackle Aeneas Peebles and quarterback Kedon Slovis. Slovis is the emergency third quarterback.

sports.title: Report: Aidan Hutchinson has torn ACL but no additional damage
sports.summary: Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson received a bit of good news after additional testing on his right knee.
sports.body:
Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that, while Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL, he has no other significant damage.

Initial reports indicated the Lions feared Hutchinson “probably” had additional damage in his knee, specifically his meniscus.

Hutchinson and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye were both injured on Hutchinson’s third-down sack of Maye with 9:28 left in the first quarter. Maye injured his ankle on the play, and the injury could be season-ending. Hutchinson injured his knee on the celebration afterward.

Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, said through a league spokesman that Hutchinson’s tackle was not an illegal hip drop .

This marks the second time in three seasons that Hutchinson’s season will end early. He finishes 2026 with six sacks.

sports.title: Mike Vrabel disagrees with Milton Williams's claim that field conditions caused injuries
sports.summary: On Sunday in Germany, both teams had key players go down with significant injuries.
sports.body:
After the game, Patriots defensive tackle Milton Williams blamed the injuries suffered by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (ankle) on the playing surface in Munich.

“Two top players in this league, probably got season-ending injuries playing on that [field],” Williams said, via Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald . “It was bad. But like I said, I ain’t making no excuses. [The Lions] executed. They played on the same field we did, and they executed and made more plays than we did. Give them credit.”

On Monday, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel disagreed with Williams’s opinion.

“I don’t think Drake Maye’s injury was caused by the grass,” Vrabel told reporters, “and certainly we’ve seen other players that have celebrated or have left their feet and come down and had issues at that. So the field was the same for both teams, and that’s kind of what the field was.”

Vrabel stopped short of commenting on whether the field was an issue independent of the injuries. But he’s right; it’s the same for both teams.

Still, we know by now that every field is different. And there’s surely a difference between American fields that host up to 10 games per year every year and the international one-off surfaces.

sports.title: The NFL's Week 12 flex decision is looming
sports.summary: Thanksgiving week will entail a smorgasbord of football.
sports.body:
The NFL’s brand-new embrace of the previously quiet night before Thanksgiving, only a few years after Black Friday was invaded, creates nine separate windows for the weekend — and seven standalone games.

The Wednesday night clash, pitting the 6-4 Packers against the 6-4 Rams, has huge implications for the slow-moving game of wild-card musical chairs in the NFC. The early Thanksgiving contest has the 7-2 Bears visiting the 7-2 Lions in a massive NFC North battle.

The Eagles-Cowboys game at 4:25 p.m. ET is becoming increasingly irrelevant — and it’ll still get more than 40 million viewers because any game in that window would generate a huge audience. The Thursday night game, between the 7-2 Chiefs and the 8-1 Bills, will be very relevant to the AFC West championship and the No. 1 seed in the conference.

On Friday, it’s the 7-2 Broncos at the 6-3 Steelers, which also has major playoff implications.

Then comes the late-afternoon Sunday window. At 4:25 p.m. ET, the 8-1 49ers host the 6-4 Seahawks.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t end there. On Sunday night, the 5-5 Patriots (who likely won’t have quarterback Drake Maye) visit the 0-8 Chargers.

If the NFL is going to slide that game out of prime time, Tuesday is the deadline for doing it. For the Eagles-Commanders game in Week 8, the league opted not to move a more consequential game into the Sunday night spot. Will the NFL again stand pat, keeping the Pats and Chargers as, to borrow a classic line from John Madden, the last shot out of a Roman candle?

The problem is that the playing of five games on Wednesday through Sunday leaves few options for Sunday night. In the 1:00 p.m. ET window, the games are Saints-Bengals, Raiders-Browns, Ravens-Texans, Giants-Colts, Jets-Dolphins, and Falcons-Vikings. Titans-Jaguars is due to begin at 4:05 p.m. ET, with Commanders-Cardinals being the other 4:25 p.m. ET game.

sports.title: Lions claim DE Tyrus Wheat off of waivers
sports.summary: The Lions lost Aidan Hutchinson for the rest of the season on Sunday and they moved to add another defensive end to the roster on Monday.
sports.body:
They announced that they have claimed Tyrus Wheat off of waivers. Wheat was let go by the Cowboys over the weekend.

It will be Wheat’s second tour of duty with the Lions. He played in 15 games for the team last season and recorded 15 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble in those appearances.

Wheat had three tackles in five games for the Cowboys this season and he also played 20 games for Dallas during the 2023 and 2024 seasons.

The Lions waived defensive back Nick Whiteside in a corresponding move.

sports.title: Giants sign WR Xavier Gipson, DB Tavierre Thomas to their active roster
sports.summary: The Giants signed wide receiver Xavier Gipson and defensive back Tavierre Thomas to their active roster on Monday, the team announced.
sports.body:
Gipson was on the Eagles’ practice squad, and Thomas was on the Vikings’ practice squad.

The Giants cut wide receiver Charlie Jones and defensive back Nikko Reed from their practice squad in corresponding moves.

The Eagles signed Gipson to their practice squad on Sept. 11 after he spent training camp with the Giants.

He has appeared in 41 regular-season games with three starts for the Jets (2023-25), Giants (2025) and Eagles (2025). Gipson has yet to appear in a game this season.

Thomas played all 17 games each of the previous two years, but has appeared in only one game this season. He made his 2026 debut last Monday night against the Bills, playing 24 snaps on special teams.

In 116 regular-season games with 22 starts for the Browns (2018-20), Texans (2021-23), Buccaneers (2024) and Vikings (2025-26). His career numbers include 193 tackles, seven forced fumbles, six tackles for loss, two forced fumbles and two interceptions.

sports.title: Raiders sign QB Brett Rypien to the practice squad
sports.summary: The Raiders needed another quarterback after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.
sports.body:
Rypien joins Fernando Mendoza and Aidan O’Connell in the quarterbacks room.

The Raiders released defensive end Bralen Trice from the practice squad to make room for Rypien.

Rypien was most recently with the Buccaneers, signing with their practice squad in September, when Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb.

Rypien, the nephew of Super Bowl XXVI MVP Mark Rypien, has appeared in games with the Broncos, Rams and Bengals. He has played 11 games, going 2-2 as a starter, but has not appeared in a game since 2023.

sports.title: Brian Schottenheimer on confidence in Christian Parker: We're still working through the process
sports.summary: One constant of the 2026 Cowboys season has been a focus on defensive coordinator Christian Parker's job security in the wake of losses and things aren't any different in the aftermath of Sunday's loss to the 49ers.
sports.body:
The 49ers piled up 584 yards and scored three touchdowns that covered at least 66 yards in their 46-40 win, which led head coach Brian Schottenheimer to call their tackling unacceptable in his postgame press conference. Executive vice president Stephen Jones used the same word to describe the team’s performance on Monday and Schottenheimer’s press conference later in the day began with a question about whether he remains confident in Parker.

“We’ll still working through the process,” Schottenheimer said. “Talking to the guys is the first step. At the end of the day, there’s a lot of things we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me. You look at this game, the positives. Five sacks team that had been sacked eight times — you get five sacks. Probably missed another three or four, could have been almost double digits. But at the end of the day, the tackling and some of the coverage stuff led to the explosives. We’re taking a deep dive, we’re looking at everything.”

The answer notably didn’t include an affirmation of confidence in Parker, which led to a followup asking if there’s a chance that they could make a change involving Parker.

“I’m not saying that. I’m saying we’re still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today,” Schottenheimer said.

The Cowboys may not choose to make a change, but it’s hard to feel confident that there’s going to be a major difference between their play over the first 10 weeks and their play over the rest of the season if everything about the defensive approach remains the same.

sports.title: The extensive officiating adjustments worked, but were they necessary?
sports.summary: Friday's nationwide ground stop didn't affect any of the NFL teams that needed to travel from one place to the other for Week 10 games.
sports.body:
But not because the officials assigned to work the various games couldn’t get to where they needed to be. The league decided to reshuffle the deck in order to avoid the mere possibility that the officials wouldn’t get to their assigned games.

It was a proactive approach by the notoriously reactive NFL. But it still may have been an overreaction. And it introduced the risk that something unusual could have occurred.

For the twelve games played on Sunday, the assigned referee worked only two of the games . One of those games was played on Sunday morning (New York time) in Germany, where travel undoubtedly occurred before Friday’s shutdown of the aviation system.

Sunday night’s game was due to be worked by Clete Blakeman as the referee, with umpire Scott Walker, down judge Andy Warner, line judge Kent Payne, field judge Karina Tovar, side judge James Coleman, back judge Jonah Monroe, replay official Chad Adams, and replay assistant Adam Choate.

Instead, from the official Game Book, this was the crew: referee Don Willard, umpire Terry Killens, down judge Dana McKenzie, line judge Jay Bilbo, field judge Jabir Walker, side judge Justin Larrew, back judge Dino Paganelli.

Chad Adams was still the replay official; however, all replay officials reportedly went to the league office and not their game sites.

Willard was not scheduled to work in Week 10; he ultimately served as the referee for two games. Killens was due to work the Jaguars-Titans game as a member of referee Alex Moore’s crew; like Willard, Killens worked Dolphins-Colts and Steelers-Bengals. McKenzie, like Killens, is a member of Moore’s crew, which was due to be in Nashville.

Bilbo is a member of referee Shawn Smith’s crew, which was due to work Panthers-Saints. Walker, who also worked two games, is a member of Land Clark’s crew, which was scheduled to work the Chargers-Ravens game on Monday night.

sports.title: Dolphins waive Jamree Kromah
sports.summary: The Dolphins have let go of an edge rusher.
sports.body:
Kromah, 26, joined the Dolphins late last month after he was claimed off waivers.

The Bears had let him go after they traded for defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons.

Kromah appeared in two games for Miami, playing two defensive snaps and 10 special teams snaps.

He could return to Miami’s roster on the practice squad if he clears waivers.

sports.title: Bucs sign QB Easton Stick from the practice squad to the active roster
sports.summary: The Buccaneers signed quarterback Easton Stick from the practice squad to the active roster on Monday, the team announced.
sports.body:
In addition, the Buccaneers signed wide receiver David Sills to the practice squad and released cornerback Brandon Johnson to make room on the 17-player unit.

The quarterback maneuvers come as Baker Mayfield deals with a lower-leg injury.

Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his fourth start of the season if Mayfield can’t play Sunday. Stick would serve as Daniels’ backup.

Stick was active for Daniels’ three starts in Weeks 4-6 as Mayfield worked his way back from a dislocated right thumb. Stick is now out of practice squad elevations.

The Bucs signed Stick to the practice squad on Aug. 31, but he has previous experience in offensive coordinator Zac Robinson’s system. The two were together in Atlanta last season.

Rush also has NFL starting experience, having opened 18 games with Dallas, Baltimore and Atlanta. That includes two starts for the Falcons this season.

Sills was on the Buccaneers’ active roster for three weeks before the team waived him Nov. 10.

Johnson was on the Buccaneers’ practice squad for five weeks. He previously saw regular-season action with the Eagles in 2025, appearing in three games with one start.

sports.title: Robert Saleh: We've put more on Cam Ward's plate and he's proving he can handle it
sports.summary: The Titans lost their third straight game on Sunday, but head coach Robert Saleh continued to like what he saw from quarterback Cam Ward during Jacksonville's 40-23 win.
sports.body:
Ward was 28-of-39 for 231 yards, two touchdowns and an interception while running three times for 39 yards. That marked a season-high in completion percentage for Ward and he has completed at least 64.5 percent of his passes in all three of the losses.

That run coincides with what Saleh called a decision to “shift our philosophy with how we wanted to approach offense and put more in his plate with regard to being a general at the line of scrimmage.” Saleh said that Ward has done “a really nice job taking command” and has shown the Titans what they were hoping to see in the process.

“To be fair to Cam, we’ve said from the beginning we were going to give him every opportunity to prove that he is a franchise quarterback of the Tennessee Titans,” Saleh said at a Monday press conference. “So, philosophically, the change was: How are we going to evaluate whether or not is he capable of being our franchise quarterback if we don’t give him the opportunity to prove it? And I think over the last three weeks he has done that. Or, at least is doing it .”

The Titans scored 84 points in their first six games and they’ve put up 83 in the three games since the tweak in their offensive approach. That step in the right direction has not resulted in wins, but it is reason to hope that will change if Ward is able to sustain the improvement that the Titans have seen over the last few weeks.

And I think said improvement can occur in Buffalo’s pass game if slot receiver Khalil Shakir becomes a focal point. I won’t fault you for questioning why I’m writing this now after Shakir had two catches for 29 yards — along with three “runs” for 26 yards — in the win over the Jets in Week 10. There are a few reasons — it’s a follow from one of my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory in MetLie Stadium, Amon-Ra St. Brown went off for the Lions against the Patriots in Germany, and Parker Washington had the most receiving yards in a game (152) for the Jaguars since 2019. Oh, and now is the ideal time to start incorporating Shakir into a more prominent role, right before the Bills have this five-game stretch during the holiday season — vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers, vs. Bears, and at Broncos. sports.body: Josh Allen has as many rushing touchdowns as Eric Dickerson. Yes, we’re comparing a quarterback to the guy who ran for 2,105 yards in one season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2122058091134881834?a=hfBRzB3qb8hT6ZX9EDw&s=20] Allen scored his 90th career rushing touchdown during Buffalo’s Week 10 game against the New York Jets, tying Dickerson and fellow Hall of Famer Curtis Martin for 14th on the NFL’s all-time list. He entered the game with 88. Number 89 came on a one yard run in the first quarter. Number 90 was a two-yard run on the Bills’ first possession of the third quarter. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2122034725476766076?a=C37X0KjNpeEIGge-adI&s=20] [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2122057732488376770?a=x6C71tZcVsvn-l8ycns&s=20] Dickerson and Martin weren’t running backs who had a few good seasons. Dickerson led the NFL in rushing four times, and nobody has topped his single-season yardage record in more than 40 years. Martin opened his career with 10 straight 1,000-yard seasons, including seven with the New York Jets. Bills fans had plenty of opportunities to get tired of watching him, but now they can celebrate one of their own making what he did look average. Both finished with 90 rushing touchdowns. Allen has matched them in his ninth season while also being responsible for, you know, throwing the football. The quarterback record is already his. It has been for a while. Now Allen has reached the point where we’re comparing his touchdown total to some of the best running backs to ever play, and he could pass a few more before this season is over. One more rushing touchdown would tie Jerome Bettis and Franco Harris for 12th at 91. Barry Sanders is next at 99, followed by Marshall Faulk and Shaun Alexander at 100. Allen would need 10 more to join that pair in ninth place, which is asking a lot. But we’re talking about a quarterback with a chance to finish the season in the NFL’s top 10 for career rushing touchdowns. We can keep asking him to slide, but we shouldn’t expect that he will. Apparently, he has a few more people to catch first.

sports.body: > “I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs.” That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the television series, The Office. Michael Scott didn’t end up losing his job as branch manager of Dunder-Mifflin in the end. Nevertheless, the review remains relatable. Sometimes people can improve their job performance, but other times you reach a realization that they just aren’t capable of doing it. We are past that stage with Aaron Glenn. We can point to any number of dubious marks of his resume as Jets head coach. He is now 5-22, sporting a worse winning percentage as an NFL head coach than Hue Jackson. Glenn now has more than twice as many double digit point losses than he has wins. The latest defeat was the ugly 31-12 blowout at the hands of the Buffalo Bills in Week 10. There isn’t much drama left surrounding Glenn. Barring an unexpected late season surge, he will not retain his job as Jets head coach for a third year. Even if there is a late season winning streak, it still might not be enough. NFL teams don’t reassign their coach to a different department. Coaching contracts aren’t written that way, and practical considerations make the sort of demotion recommended for Scott unviable. Glenn will be let go. He will make enough money to leave football if he so chooses. If he decides to continue his coaching career, he will be an in demand candidates for teams seeking a new defensive coordinator. In the meantime, we will have to endure seven more games. That will be no easy task. I am sure the Jets will invent new ways to lose along the way. At 8-1, the Bills are out to their best start since 1991. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. I’m glad we saw some pass-game pop within structure During the Bills’ four-game win streak entering this game, which included dominance after the bye week, it felt natural to narrow focus on Buffalo’s entire operation, checking for any component of the team that could improve. And in wins over the Rams, Raiders, Ravens, and Vikings, Buffalo seemingly lacked efficiency from the pass game in a classic sense. You know, Josh Allen standing in the pocket and completing the football to pass catchers within the intended design of the play. It hadn’t happened at the frequency one would expect in games in which the Bills scored 37, 33, 36, and 23 points (against the No. 1 defense in football on the road). But in the second half against the Jets, the Bills demonstrated their ability to move the ball through the air in a normal, rhythmic way… at all levels of the field. And there was an explosive element that’s been mostly missing over the past four outings. For as good as Allen has been creating this season, and for as reliable as Buffalo has been on the ground, this team needs to be able to win with classic dropback passing too, and in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets, the Bills did just that. sports.body: The New York Jets lost their fifth straight game and eighth of their last nine on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 - 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 - 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 - 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets on Sunday and with the Denver Broncos on a bye, the Bills have now opened a full one-game lead in the AFC. The Kansas City Chiefs actually pass the Broncos thanks to a superiors record in the AFC West, so Buffalo’s lead is over K.C as well as the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars. In the AFC East, the New England Patriots lost in Germany, which drops them to 5-5. The Bills have a 3-game lead in the division and the Patriots have games against the Bills, Vikings, Chiefs, and Broncos still upcoming. With so many games going on still here, we will update but the headline won’t change; the Bills have a playoff picture stranglehold. Explaining the 7-2 tiebreakers in the AFC The Chiefs and Broncos first go to a divisional tiebreaker at 7-2, where Kansas City wins with a 3-1 record in the AFC West over the Broncos at 2-1. Kansas City is the division leader. The Chiefs, Jaguars, and Bengals go into a three-way tiebreaker and one team hasn’t beat all the others, so it heads to AFC record. Kansas City wins with a 6-1 AFC record to secure the two seed. Then the Jaguars have a head-to-head win over Cincinnati to nab the three seed. The Broncos slot in as the top Wild Card. sports.body: In the New York Jets’ 10th game of the 2026 season, on a breezy, chilly November day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Buffalo Bills blew out the Jets, 31 - 12. The game opened with the Jets on defense. The Bills advanced past midfield before they were forced to punt. The Jets then went nowhere and were forced to punt out of their own end zone. The Bills then went on a long, grinding drive ending in a Josh Allen quarterback sneak for a touchdown and a 7 - 0 Bills lead late in the first quarter. The first quarter ended with the score still Bills 7, Jets 0. The Jets had the ball in Bills territory. On third down and 14 the Jets did a Jets thing, throwing well short of the sticks to Mason Taylor. They settled for a short field goal to make the score 7 - 3 in favor of the Bills. Shades of last week against the Chiefs when the Jets constantly settled for field goals against a team they knew would score often against them. Trying to make the score respectable rather than trying to win. The Bills came right back with a scoring drive of their own. They narrowly missed a touchdown when James Cook dropped a perfect pass that likely would have ended in Cook scoring. Instead the Bills settled for a field goal and a 10 - 3 lead midway through the second quarter. Neither team got anything going again on offense until the Jets put together a drive featuring some nice Geno Smith to Garrett Wilson connections late in the quarter. The drive stalled inside the Bills 20 yard line and the Jets settled for another field goal with less than 20 seconds left in the half. The Jets went into the locker room trailing the Bills 10 - 6. The Jets opened the third quarter on offense. Geno Smith was on the sideline with an injury he incurred at he end of the first half. Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut at quarterback for the Jets. Klubnik put together a nice drive to open the second half, using his legs to run for a couple of first downs and finding Garrett Wilson for a long completion. Unfortunately, the drive stalled deep in Bills territory. The Jets had to again settle for a field goal, making the score Bills 10, Jets 9. The Jets momentum was fleeting. At this point in a lost season, fans frequently are ready to see a younger quarterback go into the lineup and get some reps. Most Jets fans haven’t reached that point, though, at least according to our most recent SB Nation Reacts poll. We asked whether it was Cade Klubnik time.
